newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Gov. proposes $19.2 bln operating budget.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Gov. proposes $19.2 bln operating budget.

text.p: Washington state Gov. Gary Locke on Tuesday proposed a $19.2 billion operating budget for the 1997-1999 biennium that leaves a reserve of $304 million.
Locke said his financial plan stresses public education, protects working families and the environment and provides tax relief to homeowners and businesses.
The proposal offers the smallest percentage increase in the state's budget in more than 25 years, and comes in under state spending limits, the governor said.

"We've taken a comprehensive approach to building this budget," Locke said. "We're tightening our belts and making tough choices so that we can direct new dollars toward my number one priority, education."

Locke dedicated $11.2 billion of his budget to education. He earmarked nearly $70 million to raise academic standards through student grants for local school districts and added $17.3 million to assist property tax-poor school districts.

Locke said his budget would provide $39 million to implement local watershed plans and would lay the groundwork for long-term solutions to the state's water problems. He also earmarked $50 million for the Washington Wildlife and Recreation Program, and said he would fund the Trust Land Transfer Program at $31 million.

The governor's tax relief measures would provide $311 million in tax reductions for homeowners and businesses during the next two years. He pledged to return business and occupation tax rates to pre-1993 levels by cutting business taxes $94 million and property taxes by $217 million.
Locke said his budget plan would provide $75 million to address the current shortfall in the state's Health Services Account, which subsidizes medical coverage for families.

His budget would provide $366.8 million for cost-of-living adjustments for teachers, faculty members and all other state employees. Teachers, university faculty and other state employees would receive a 2.5 percent raise each year.

Under Locke's welfare reform plan, total funding for child care would be more than $330 million. Locke earmarked $121 million in state funds to help those facing the loss of federal Supplemental Security Income and food stamps.
The focus of the Locke's 10-year capital plan is public education, which would receive 54 percent of the funds available for new construction in the 1997-1999 biennium.

His capital plan includes $116 million to begin a branch-campus construction program. The capital plan would fully fund anticipated public school construction needs over the next 10 years, the governor said.
